questions.q: What will happen to the bones of the people?
questions.a: People will spread the bones all over the ground.

questions.q: Will those who are alive wish they could live or wish they could die?
questions.a: They will wish they could die.

questions.q: What do people who are lost try to do?
questions.a: They try to find their way again.

questions.q: What do the people of Jerusalem refuse to do?
questions.a: They refuse to turn away from their deceitful ways and change their behavior.

questions.q: How did the people feel about their wickedness?
questions.a: No one regretted his wickedness.

questions.q: How are Yahweh’s people not like birds?
questions.a: Birds know what they are supposed to do, but his people do not know Yahweh’s decrees.

questions.q: What have the scribes done?
questions.a: They have written things that deceive the people.

questions.q: What will happen to the wise ones who rejected the word of Yahweh?
questions.a: They will be put to shame, dismayed, and captured by their enemies.

questions.q: What will Yahweh do with their wives and their fields?
questions.a: He will give their wives and fields to other people.

questions.q: What do the leaders falsely tell the people?
questions.a: They tell the people that there will be peace, but there will be no peace.

questions.q: Were the people ashamed because of their sins?
questions.a: No, they were not ashamed.

questions.q: What will Yahweh do because they were not ashamed?
questions.a: He will have their enemies kill them.

questions.q: What will happen to the grapes and figs?
questions.a: There will be no grapes on the vine and no figs on the fig tree; the leaves will wither.

questions.q: What do the people decide to do?
questions.a: They decide to go to the cities and die there.

questions.q: What happened instead of the peace and healing the people hoped for?
questions.a: Terror came instead.

questions.q: What will the enemy’s horses do?
questions.a: They will come and consume the land and everything in it, the city and the people living there.

questions.q: What is Yahweh sending to harm them?
questions.a: He is sending enemy soldiers like poisonous snakes to harm them.

questions.q: How does Jeremiah feel?
questions.a: He feels very sad and faint in his heart.

questions.q: Where is Yahweh?
questions.a: Yahweh is in Zion.

questions.q: Where are the people who are screaming?
questions.a: They are in a land far away.

questions.q: What has Yahweh not done, even though the harvest and summer have ended?
questions.a: Yahweh has not rescued the people from their enemies.

questions.q: How does Jeremiah feel because of what has happened to his people?
questions.a: He is broken, mourns, and is completely dismayed.

questions.q: What does Jeremiah ask about the land of Gilead?
questions.a: He asks whether there is medicine and a doctor there to heal his people.

commentary.text: The remains of the dead exposed. (Jer. 8:1-3) The stupidity of the people, compared with the instinct of the brute creation. (Jer. 8:4-13) The alarm of the invasion, and lamentation. (Jer. 8:14-22)

Jer. 8:1-3 Though no real hurt can be done to a dead body, yet disgrace to the remains of wicked persons may alarm those yet alive; and this reminds us that the Divine justice and punishments extend beyond the grave. Whatever befalls us here, let us humble ourselves before God, and seek his mercy.

Jer. 8:4-13 What brought this ruin? 1. The people would not attend to reason; they would not act in the affairs of their souls with common prudence. Sin is backsliding; it is going back from the way that leads to life, to that which leads to destruction. 2. They would not attend to the warning of conscience. They did not take the first step towards repentance: true repentance begins in serious inquiry as to what we have done, from conviction that we have done amiss. 3. They would not attend to the ways of providence, nor understand the voice of God in them, Jer. 8:7. They know not how to improve the seasons of grace, which God affords. Many boast of their religious knowledge, yet, unless taught by the Spirit of God, the instinct of brutes is a more sure guide than their supposed wisdom. 4. They would not attend to the written word. Many enjoy abundance of the means of grace, have Bibles and ministers, but they have them in vain. They will soon be ashamed of their devices. The pretenders to wisdom were the priests and the false prophets. They flattered people in sin, and so flattered them into destruction, silencing their fears and complaints with, All is well. Selfish teachers may promise peace when there is no peace; and thus men encourage each other in committing evil; but in the day of visitation they will have no refuge to flee unto.

Jer. 8:14-22 At length they begin to see the hand of God lifted up. And when God appears against us, every thing that is against us appears formidable. As salvation only can be found in the Lord, so the present moment should be seized. Is there no medicine proper for a sick and dying kingdom? Is there no skilful, faithful hand to apply the medicine? Yes, God is able to help and to heal them. If sinners die of their wounds, their blood is upon their own heads. The blood of Christ is balm in Gilead, his Spirit is the Physician there, all-sufficient; so that the people may be healed, but will not. Thus men die unpardoned and unchanged, for they will not come to Christ to be saved.
